results.title: Surjectivity of the residue map for a singly generated algebra
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings, $B$ an $A$-algebra, $\mathfrak q$ an ideal of $B$ and $\mathfrak p$ its preimage under $A \to B$. If $B$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by a single element $\pi \in \mathfrak q$, then the canonical map $A/\mathfrak p \to B/\mathfrak q$ is surjective.

results.title: Inertia degree one for a singly generated algebra
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings, $B$ an $A$-algebra, and $\mathfrak q$ a maximal ideal of $B$ whose preimage $\mathfrak p$ under $A \to B$ is maximal. If $B$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by a single element $\pi \in \mathfrak q$, then the inertia degree of $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$ is $1$.

results.title: Generalized tau function

results.summary: For a subset $F \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, its affine dimension is the dimension of the real vector space spanned by the differences $x - y$ with $x, y \in F$. The empty set and every single point get dimension $0$.

results.title: Flag of a convex polytope
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A flag of a convex polytope $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a sequence $F_0, F_1, \dots, F_{n-1}$ of faces of $P$ such that each $F_k$ has affine dimension $k$ and $F_i \subsetneq F_j$ whenever $i < j$.

results.title: Rigid motions
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The rigid motions of $\mathbb{R}^n$ are the affine isometric bijections $\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Symmetry of a convex polytope
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An affine isometry $\varphi$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a symmetry of a convex polytope $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ if $\varphi(P) = P$.

results.title: Regular convex polytope
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A convex polytope $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is regular (Platonic) if it is full-dimensional and for any two flags $(F_0, \dots, F_{n-1})$ and $(G_0, \dots, G_{n-1})$ of $P$ there is an affine isometry $\varphi$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\varphi(P) = P$ and $\varphi(F_k) = G_k$ for every $k < n$.

results.title: Similar polytopes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two convex polytopes $P$ and $Q$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ are similar when there are a real number $a > 0$ and an affine isometry $\varphi$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that the underlying set of $Q$ is $\{a\,\varphi(x) : x \in P\}$.

results.title: Regular polytopes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the set of regular (Platonic) convex polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^d$: the convex polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that are full-dimensional and whose symmetry group acts transitively on their flags.

results.title: Similarity of regular polytopes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For regular convex polytopes $P$ and $Q$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $P$ is related to $Q$ when they are similar as convex polytopes, that is, when there are a real number $a > 0$ and an affine isometry $\varphi$ of $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that the underlying set of $Q$ is $\{a\,\varphi(x) : x \in P\}$.

results.title: Number of Platonic polytopes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, $p_d \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is the number of similarity classes of regular convex polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^d$, with $p_d = \infty$ when there are infinitely many classes.

results.title: Classification of the Platonic polytopes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$ let $p_d \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ be the number of regular convex polytopes in $\mathbb{R}^d$ up to similarity. Then $p_2 = \infty$, $p_3 = 5$, $p_4 = 6$, and $p_d = 3$ for every $d \ge 5$.

results.title: Scottish Book Problem 88 (Mazur)

results.summary: The claim that every real sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with the following property satisfies $\sum_n n |a_n| < \infty$: for every real sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $|x_n| \le 1$ for all $n$, each series $\sum_n a_{m+n} x_n$ with $m \ge 0$ converges, as the limit of its partial sums, to some $L_m$, and $\sum_m |L_m| < \infty$.

results.title: Lower bound for a power sum at the mean exponent

results.title: Power mean bound for power sums with a smaller exponent
results.caption: Theorem

results.summary: Let $F_k$ denote the $k$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. results.title: Height change of a colored Motzkin step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The height change of an admissible step of rank $r$ is the integer $j + 1$ for an up-step $U_j$ with $0 \le j < r$, $0$ for a level step, and $-(j + 1)$ for a down-step $D_j$ with $0 \le j < r$, whatever its color.

results.title: Height of a colored step sequence after k steps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $p = (p_0, \dots, p_{n-1})$ of $n$ admissible steps of rank $r$ and a natural number $k$, the height of $p$ after $k$ steps is the integer $\sum_{i < \min(k, n)} h(p_i)$, where $h$ is the height change of a step. For $k \ge n$ it is the height of the whole sequence.

results.title: Colored Motzkin path condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $r \ge 1$. A sequence $p = (p_0, \dots, p_{n-1})$ of $n$ admissible steps of rank $r$ is a Motzkin path when its height after $k$ steps is nonnegative for every $k$ with $0 \le k \le n$ and its height after $n$ steps is $0$.

results.title: Colored Motzkin paths of rank r and length n
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $r \ge 1$ and a natural number $n$, the colored Motzkin paths of rank $r$ and length $n$ are the sequences $(p_0, \dots, p_{n-1})$ of $n$ admissible steps of rank $r$ that satisfy the Motzkin path condition: the height after $k$ steps is nonnegative for every $k \le n$, and the height after $n$ steps is $0$.

results.title: (u,l,d)-Motzkin numbers of rank r
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $l$ be natural numbers and let $u, d \colon \{0, \dots, r - 1\} \to \mathbb{N}$. For a natural number $n$, the $(u,l,d)$-Motzkin number of rank $r$ and length $n$ is the number of colored Motzkin paths of rank $r$ and length $n$ whose up-steps $U_j$ come in $u(j)$ colors, whose level steps come in $l$ colors, and whose down-steps $D_j$ come in $d(j)$ colors.

results.title: The (u,l,d)-Motzkin number counts Motzkin step sequences

results.title: Encoded DFA
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An encoded deterministic finite automaton over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a deterministic finite automaton given as data with natural-number states: a start state in $\mathbb{N}$, a list of accepting states in $\mathbb{N}$, and a list of transitions $((s, a), t)$ with $s, t \in \mathbb{N}$ and $a \in \alpha$, read as "on letter $a$, state $s$ moves to $t$".

results.title: Transition function of an encoded DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$, a state $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and a letter $a$, the step of $D$ from $s$ on $a$ is the target of the first transition that $D$ lists from $s$ on $a$, or $s$ itself when $D$ lists no such transition.

results.title: The automaton denoted by an encoded DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ denotes the deterministic automaton over $\alpha$ with state set $\mathbb{N}$ whose start state is the start state of $D$, whose transition function is the transition function of $D$, and whose accepting states are the states in the accepting list of $D$.

results.title: Language of an encoded DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The language of an encoded DFA $D$ is the set of words $w$ such that the state reached by running $D$ on $w$ from its start state, following its transition function, is one of its accepting states.

results.title: Letters of an encoded DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The letters of an encoded DFA $D$ form the list of the letters $a$ of its listed transitions $((s, a), t)$, in the order the transitions are listed.

results.title: States of an encoded DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The states of an encoded DFA $D$ form the list consisting of its start state followed by the targets of its listed transitions, in the order they are listed.

results.title: Unlisted transitions fix the state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA, $s \in \mathbb{N}$ a state and $a$ a letter. If $D$ lists no transition from $s$ on $a$, then the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ to $s$.

results.title: A step determined by its listed transitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA, let $s, t \in \mathbb{N}$ be states and let $a$ be a letter. If $D$ lists at least one transition from $s$ on $a$, and every transition listed from $s$ on $a$ has target $t$, then the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ to $t$.

results.title: Letters without listed transitions fix every state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA and let $a$ be a letter that is not among the letters of $D$, that is, no listed transition of $D$ is labelled $a$. Then for every state $s \in \mathbb{N}$ the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ to $s$.

results.title: Where a step can lead
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded DFA $D$, state $s \in \mathbb{N}$ and letter $a$, the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ either to the target of some listed transition of $D$ or to $s$ itself.

results.title: The listed states are closed under transitions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA and let $s$ be one of its states, that is, its start state or the target of one of its listed transitions. Then for every letter $a$ the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ on $a$ to one of the states of $D$.

results.title: Complement of an encoded DFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The complement of an encoded DFA $D$ has the same start state and the same transitions as $D$, and its accepting states are those states of $D$ (its start state and the targets of its listed transitions) that $D$ does not accept.

results.title: The complement DFA accepts the complement language
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded DFA $D$ and every word $w$, the complement of $D$ accepts $w$ if and only if $D$ does not accept $w$.

results.title: Every finite DFA has an encoding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states has an encoded DFA with the same language.

results.title: Encoded DFAs as triples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Sending an encoded DFA over $\alpha$ to the triple of its start state, its list of accepting states and its list of transitions is an equivalence (a bijection with explicit inverse) between encoded DFAs over $\alpha$ and the set $\mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{List}\,\mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{List}((\mathbb{N} \times \alpha) \times \mathbb{N})$.

results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an alphabet with a primitive recursive encoding and decidable equality, and encode encoded DFAs over $\alpha$ through their start state, accepting states and transitions. results.title: Encoded NFA
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An encoded NFA over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a nondeterministic finite automaton with ε-moves given as data, with natural numbers as states: a list of start states, a list of accepting states, a list of transitions $((s, a), t)$, meaning that on the letter $a$ the state $s$ may move to $t$, and a list of ε-moves $(s, t)$, meaning that the state $s$ may move to $t$ without reading a letter.

results.title: The ε-NFA of an encoded NFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An encoded NFA $N$ over $\alpha$ denotes the ε-NFA over $\alpha$ with state set $\mathbb{N}$ whose start states are the start states listed in $N$, whose accepting states are the accepting states listed in $N$, and in which a state $s$ may move to $t$ on a letter $a$ exactly when $((s, a), t)$ is a transition of $N$, and without reading a letter exactly when $(s, t)$ is an ε-move of $N$.

results.title: Language of an encoded NFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The language of an encoded NFA $N$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ is the language accepted by the ε-NFA that $N$ denotes, whose states are the natural numbers: the words $w$ over $\alpha$ such that some accepting state of $N$ is among the states reached on $w$ from the start states of $N$, with ε-moves allowed before, between and after the letters.

results.title: States an encoded NFA mentions as start states or targets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, this is the list of the start states of $N$, followed by the targets $t$ of its transitions $((s, a), t)$, followed by the targets $t$ of its ε-moves $(s, t)$.

results.title: ε-move relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, the ε-move relation holds between states $s$ and $t$ exactly when $(s, t)$ is one of the ε-moves of $N$.

results.title: The ε-closure is reachability along ε-moves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, a set $X$ of natural numbers and a natural number $t$, $t$ lies in the ε-closure of $X$ in the ε-NFA that $N$ denotes if and only if $t$ is reachable from some $u \in X$ by a sequence of zero or more ε-moves of $N$.

results.title: ε-successors of a state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a state $s$, the ε-successors of $s$ are the list of the targets $t$ of the ε-moves $(s, t)$ of $N$, in the order in which these ε-moves are listed.

results.title: ε-closure of a list of states
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a list $S$ of states, the ε-closure of $S$ is a list whose members are exactly the states reachable from some state of $S$ by finitely many ε-moves of $N$ (zero moves included), computed by a search from each state of $S$.

results.title: Letter step of an encoded NFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, a list $S$ of states and a letter $a$, the letter step lists the target $t$ of every transition $((s, a), t)$ of $N$ with $s \in S$, in the order of the transition list of $N$, without taking the ε-closure.

results.title: One step of an encoded NFA on a list of states
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, a list $S$ of states and a letter $a$, the list of states reached from $S$ on $a$: the ε-closure, computed as a list, of the list of states $t$ such that $((s, a), t)$ is a transition of $N$ for some $s$ in $S$.

results.title: Run of an encoded NFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a word $w = a_1 \cdots a_n$, the run of $N$ on $w$ is the list of states obtained by starting from the ε-closure of the start states of $N$ and, for each letter $a_i$ in turn, taking the letter step on $a_i$ and then the ε-closure.

results.title: Membership test for encoded NFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a word $w$, the membership test is the Boolean that is true exactly when some state reached on $w$ is an accepting state of $N$. The states reached on $w$ are computed from the ε-closure of the start states by, for each letter of $w$ in turn, following the transitions on that letter and taking the ε-closure.

results.title: The run of an encoded NFA agrees with ε-NFA evaluation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, a word $w$ and a natural number $t$, $t$ is among the states in the run of $N$ on $w$ if and only if $t$ is among the states that the ε-NFA denoted by $N$ reaches on $w$ from its start states, with ε-moves allowed before, between and after the letters.

results.title: Correctness of the NFA membership test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a word $w$, the membership test returns true on $w$ if and only if $w$ belongs to the language of $N$.

results.title: The states reached on a word are closed under ε-moves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ be an encoded NFA and $w$ a word. If $u$ is one of the states that the ε-NFA denoted by $N$ can be in after reading $w$, and $N$ has an ε-move from $u$ to $v$, then $v$ is also one of these states.

results.title: Successors of a state in an encoded NFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a state $s$, this is the list of the targets $t$ of the transitions $((s, a), t)$ of $N$ on any letter $a$, followed by the targets $t$ of the ε-moves $(s, t)$ of $N$, each in the order of the corresponding list of $N$.

results.title: Reachable states of an encoded NFA
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, this is the list, found by a search from each start state of $N$ in turn through the start states of $N$ and the targets of its transitions and ε-moves, of the states reachable from a start state of $N$ by zero or more moves, each a transition of $N$ on some letter or an ε-move of $N$.

results.title: The reachable states are those some word can lead to
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$ and a natural number $t$, $t$ is among the reachable states of $N$ if and only if there is a word $w$ such that $t$ is among the states that the ε-NFA denoted by $N$ reaches on $w$ from its start states, with ε-moves allowed before, between and after the letters.

results.title: Emptiness test for encoded NFAs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded NFA $N$, the emptiness test is the Boolean that is true exactly when no state in the list of reachable states of $N$ is an accepting state of $N$; the reachable states are those reachable from a start state of $N$ by zero or more moves, each a transition on some letter or an ε-move.

results.title: Every finite ε-NFA has an encoding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An `εNFA` over a finite alphabet with finitely many states has an encoded NFA with the same language.

results.title: Every finite NFA has an encoding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An NFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states has an encoded NFA with the same language.

results.title: Encoded NFAs as tuples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bijection between encoded NFAs over $\alpha$ and quadruples consisting of a list of natural numbers, a list of natural numbers, a list of elements of $(\mathbb{N} \times \alpha) \times \mathbb{N}$ and a list of pairs of natural numbers, which sends an encoded NFA to its start states, accepting states, transitions and ε-moves.

results.title: Membership for NFAs is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(N, w)$, where $N$ is an encoded NFA (with ε-moves) over $\alpha$ and $w$ is a word over $\alpha$, that $w$ is in the language of $N$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is Sipser, Theorem 4.2: the problem $A_{\mathrm{NFA}}$ is decidable.

results.title: Emptiness of NFAs is decidable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded NFA $N$ (with ε-moves) over $\alpha$ that its language is empty is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $E_{\mathrm{NFA}}$.
